retro:
# Retrospective

## What worked

Fresh reviewer sessions and equivalent neutral tasks produced independent production-script reproductions. Replaying a desktop file generated by the old installer exposed the persistent-state transition without needing a real browser. Source-pinned Chromium parser and consumer research made alternate-switch claims concrete. Five sealed command runs completed without setup failures and were verified at synthesis.

## Avoidable friction and improvements

The launcher exposes reviewer-specific lifecycle through its Team.start API but not a dedicated CLI command; this round used that API only for fable/astra, never whole-team ensure/assign or coordinator reset. A reviewer-only reset subcommand would make the safe path more discoverable. No confirmed launcher bug occurred.

A shared Git object store emitted commit-graph warnings; clean identity/archive checks still passed. This was nonblocking and is not attributed to the PR.

Fable included an incidental read-only host browser process observation. It was not needed for source or isolated-fixture evidence and was excluded from synthesis claims. Future neutral tasks should explicitly discourage incidental host process inspection unrelated to owned runtime cleanup, even when read-only.

## Carry forward

Keep persistent user artifacts in compatibility tests, not just fresh-install output. Distinguish guard spelling gaps from exploitable attacker paths. Preserve meaningful mocked-effect and source-only limits. Omit generic test advice and cosmetic observations from substantive public feedback.

No Omadev session was allocated or used. No confirmed Omadev issue, desktop screenshot or browser-backed validation exists for this round. Private fixture runtime state was removed by sandbox teardown; sources and evidence remain preserved.
comment:
Two issues remain at `5014fe298933`: existing Sunshine shortcuts need an upgrade transition, and equivalent Chromium switch spellings escape the new guard.

**Verified:** Fresh Sunshine installation now writes and invokes the admin command without `--ignore-certificate-errors`. The tested canonical denied arguments stop before browser dispatch; ordinary URL launches remain unchanged.

## Existing Sunshine Admin shortcuts stop launching

The old installer writes a persistent `Sunshine Admin.desktop` containing the now-refused flag. The PR changes future installations but includes no migration for that file. Replaying its generated command against the patched launcher produced:

```text
Existing entry: URL + --ignore-certificate-errors -> exit 1, no browser dispatch
Fresh entry:   URL only                          -> browser dispatch
```

This comparison executes the production scripts with browser dispatch stubbed.

**Impact:** Previously installed Sunshine Admin shortcuts fail until repaired or recreated. This concerns opening the admin page, not Sunshine streaming or server operation.

**Suggested change:** Add a narrowly scoped, idempotent migration removing the obsolete flag from the known generated Sunshine Admin command, preserving unrelated customizations. Keep the guard's refusal behavior and test the repaired old entry.

## Equivalent switch spellings escape the guard

`bin/omarchy-launch-webapp:19-24` matches literal argument spellings rather than Chromium switch names. Production-script argument capture showed:

| Extra argument | Patched launcher |
| --- | --- |
| `--ignore-certificate-errors` | Refuses |
| `-ignore-certificate-errors` | Forwards |
| `--no-sandbox` | Refuses |
| `--no-sandbox=1` | Forwards |

Chromium's [POSIX parser](https://github.com/chromium/chromium/blob/c437277394832d12031fc109ba0a6797dbfccd4c/base/command_line.cc#L60-L114) accepts both prefixes and separates `=value`. Its [certificate-error setting](https://github.com/chromium/chromium/blob/c437277394832d12031fc109ba0a6797dbfccd4c/components/network_session_configurator/browser/network_session_configurator.cc#L831-L837) and [sandbox selection](https://github.com/chromium/chromium/blob/c437277394832d12031fc109ba0a6797dbfccd4c/sandbox/policy/sandbox_type.cc#L189-L192) check switch presence, so those alternate forms retain the relevant meaning. Browser-side effects were source-inspected, not executed.

**Impact:** The preventive guard misses valid spellings of the switches it intends to exclude. No current in-tree caller using those alternate forms or attacker-driven trigger was identified; the fresh Sunshine command is fixed.

**Suggested change:** Normalize the accepted prefixes and separate optional values before matching denied switch names, retaining the exact-name distinction for `ignore-certificate-errors-spki-list`. Cover the demonstrated alternate forms alongside canonical refusals.

---

## Review information

**Test scope:** Production shell scripts with synthetic browser entries and stubbed browser/service/package effects, baseline-generated shortcut replay, existing shell tests, and pinned Chromium source inspection. No real browser TLS, certificate interstitial, singleton launch-order, Sunshine service, or complete upgrade test was performed.

**Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

**Automated AI review:** Astra initial inspection, independent Fable 5.1 and separate Astra technical reviews, followed by synthesis and verification of claims against saved targeted evidence.
